---
title: "orthologr with COAL: a tutorial"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{orthologr with COAL: a tutorial}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
---

```{r setup, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
options(width = 110)
library(orthologr)
has_diamond <- nzchar(Sys.which("diamond"))
has_perl    <- nzchar(Sys.which("perl"))
has_kaks    <- nzchar(Sys.which("KaKs_Calculator"))
has_clustalo <- nzchar(Sys.which("clustalo"))
has_coalr   <- requireNamespace("coalr", quietly = TRUE)
# coalr's own GY method (maximum likelihood) is in coalr >= 0.6.0
has_coalr_gy <- has_coalr && is.element("GY", coalr::coal_info()$methods)
# Part 3 uses four Chlamydia genomes from NCBI (1.4 MB). The chunks that need them run when the environment
# variable ORTHOLOGR_TUTORIAL_DATA names a folder for them (they are downloaded there once); the package build does
# not set it, so that building the package needs no network.
tut_dir     <- Sys.getenv("ORTHOLOGR_TUTORIAL_DATA")
get_genomes <- nzchar(tut_dir) && has_diamond && has_coalr
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  comment = "#>",
  collapse = TRUE,
  error = FALSE,
  tidy = FALSE,
  eval = has_diamond)
```

This tutorial shows how to estimate dN, dS and dN/dS of orthologous genes with **orthologr**, first on its own and
then with **COAL** working inside it, and ends with a worked example on four bacterial genomes. It is written for
someone who knows R but neither package. Every code chunk was run to make this document; the output under each
chunk is what it printed (long tables are cut with `head()`).

It covers the fork of orthologr at [Plumat-COAL/orthologr](https://github.com/Plumat-COAL/orthologr) (branch
`integration/all`, version `r packageVersion("orthologr")`), which is where COAL support lives, and COAL's R package
**coalr** `r if (has_coalr) as.character(packageVersion("coalr")) else "(not installed when this was built)"`.

# 1. What the two packages do

**orthologr** answers "which genes of species A and species B are orthologs, and how fast have they diverged?".
For two CDS (coding sequence) files it

1. translates the CDS and finds orthologs with DIAMOND (or BLAST+): best hits (`"BH"`) or reciprocal best hits
   (`"RBH"`, the default);
2. aligns the two proteins of each gene pair (Needleman-Wunsch, BLOSUM62);
3. turns each protein alignment into a codon alignment (the job of PAL2NAL);
4. estimates dN and dS from each codon alignment (Comeron's method by default; Li's method; or one of the
   KaKs_Calculator methods NG, LWL, LPB, MLWL, MLPB, YN, MYN, GY, ...);

and returns one table with a row per gene pair. Around this it has orthogroups of several species
(`orthogroups()`), DIAMOND DeepClust clusters (`deepclust()`), divergence strata (`divergence_stratigraphy()`) and
filters (`filter_dNdS()`).

**COAL** is a re-implementation of steps 2 to 4 in C++: a protein aligner, a codon threader that produces the same
codon alignments as PAL2NAL (byte for byte), and the Ka/Ks methods of KaKs_Calculator plus orthologr's Comeron and
Li. Its R package **coalr** runs that code inside the R process, on several threads, without starting a program per
gene pair and without writing files.

How they fit together:

```text
             orthologr                                   with COAL (coalr installed)
CDS files ──► DIAMOND / BLAST ortholog search ──────────► same search (orthologr)
               │
               ├─ per gene pair (engine = "orthologr"):     ─ all pairs in one batch (engine = "coal"):
               │   protein alignment   pwalign (R)            protein alignment   COAL (C++, pwalign's scoring)
               │   codon alignment     PAL2NAL (Perl)  ──►    codon alignment     COAL (same alignment as PAL2NAL)
               │                       or COAL                Ka/Ks               COAL (Comeron, Li, NG, ..., MYN)
               │   dN/dS               gestimator (C++), seqinr,
               │                       KaKs_Calculator, or COAL
               ▼                                             ▼
          one tibble per run: query_id, subject_id, dN, dS, dNdS, the hit columns, status
```

There are three levels of using COAL:

| What you set | What COAL does | Results |
|---|---|---|
| nothing (coalr installed) | codon alignments in place of PAL2NAL (`codon_aln_tool = "coal"` is the default then) | identical |
| `kaks_tool = "coal"` | also the KaKs_Calculator methods (NG ... MYN) in place of the KaKs_Calculator program | same values, no external program |
| `engine = "coal"` or `dNdS_coal()` | protein alignment, codon alignment and dN/dS for all pairs in one call, on `comp_cores` threads | same table, several times faster |

# 2. Installation

## orthologr (the fork)

orthologr needs R >= 4.4 and the Bioconductor packages Biostrings and pwalign:

```{r install-orthologr, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(c("BiocManager", "remotes"))
BiocManager::install(c("Biostrings", "pwalign"))
remotes::install_github("Plumat-COAL/orthologr@integration/all")
```

It compiles C++ code (Comeron's method), so it needs a compiler: Rtools on Windows, the Xcode command line tools on
macOS.

## coalr (COAL's R package)

coalr is not on CRAN and the COAL release on GitHub has no R package file among its assets; it is installed from
the source in COAL's repository. Pin it to the release tag so that you get the version this tutorial used:

```{r install-coalr, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("Plumat-COAL/COAL", subdir = "packaging/r/coalr", ref = "v0.6.0")
```

It needs a C++17 compiler and Rcpp, nothing else: no Python, no Perl, no external program. (COAL also has a Python
command line, `coal`, with its own pipeline; it is not needed for anything in this tutorial.)

## External programs

| Program | Needed for | How to get it |
|---|---|---|
| DIAMOND >= 2.1 | every ortholog search (`dNdS()`, `orthologs()`, `orthogroups()`, `deepclust()`) | `orthologr::diamond_install()` (downloads the official release into a user cache folder that orthologr finds), or `conda install -c bioconda diamond` |
| Perl | PAL2NAL (when coalr is not installed or `codon_aln_tool = "pal2nal"`) | on the PATH on Linux and macOS; Strawberry Perl on Windows |
| PAL2NAL | the same | bundled with orthologr (`system.file("pal2nal", package = "orthologr")`) |
| KaKs_Calculator 2.0 | the methods NG ... MYN with the default `kaks_tool`, and GY, GMYN, MS, MA, ALL | `conda install -c bioconda kakscalculator2` |
| Clustal Omega or MAFFT | multiple alignments of orthogroups and clusters (`dNdS_orthogroups()`, `dNdS_clusters()`) | `conda install -c bioconda clustalo mafft` |

```{r diamond-install, eval = FALSE}
orthologr::diamond_install()   # once; verifies the download against the release's checksum
```

## Checking the setup

orthologr has no single "check my setup" function, but the pieces are quick to look at. Which programs are found:

```{r setup-check-tools, eval = TRUE}
Sys.which(c("diamond", "perl", "KaKs_Calculator", "clustalo", "mafft"))
```

```{r setup-check-diamond}
diamond_path()   # NULL: DIAMOND is on the PATH; otherwise the folder diamond_install() used (an error if neither)
```

What COAL brings (versions, methods, genetic codes):

```{r setup-check-coal, eval = has_coalr}
packageVersion("coalr")
info <- coalr::coal_info()
names(info)
info$coal_version
info$methods
"comeron_min_sites_positive" %in% info$features   # orthologr checks this feature of a recent coalr
```

and a tiny run whose record names every program that was used (more on the record in section 6):

```{r setup-check-run}
q20 <- system.file("seqs/ortho_thal_cds.fasta", package = "orthologr")   # 20 genes of Arabidopsis thaliana
s20 <- system.file("seqs/ortho_lyra_cds.fasta", package = "orthologr")   # their orthologs in A. lyrata
res20 <- dNdS(q20, s20)
str(attr(res20, "orthologr_run")$tools)
attr(res20, "orthologr_run")$arguments$codon_aln_tool
```

# 3. Part 1: orthologr on its own

The package ships two pairs of CDS files of *Arabidopsis thaliana* and *A. lyrata*: 20 genes, and 1,000 genes.
They are real genes of the two genomes, which diverged about 10 million years ago.

## Orthologs between two species

`orthologs()` runs only the search. With CDS files say `seq_type = "cds"` (they are translated first):

```{r orthologs}
o <- orthologs(query_file = q20, subject_files = s20, seq_type = "cds")
dim(o)
head(o[, c("query_id", "subject_id", "perc_identity", "alig_length", "evalue", "bit_score")], 5)
```

`"DIAMOND_RBH"` (reciprocal best hits) is the default. Best hits are chosen by bit score (the rule of 0.4.3 was the
e-value; `best_hit_rule = "evalue"` restores it).

## dN/dS with the default method (Comeron)

`dNdS()` does the whole pipeline. The default method is Comeron's (1995), computed by C++ code inside orthologr, so
no external program is needed apart from DIAMOND (and Perl for PAL2NAL if coalr is not installed):

```{r dnds-default}
res20
```

The columns:

- `query_id`, `subject_id`: the gene pair (IDs exactly as in the FASTA headers, up to the first space);
- `dN`, `dS`, `dNdS`: the estimates; dN/dS < 1 means purifying selection, about 1 neutral evolution, > 1 positive
  selection (as an average over the whole gene);
- the columns of the DIAMOND hit table (identity, alignment length, coordinates, e-value, bit score);
- `status`, the last column: how each pair came out (`"ok"`, `"dS_zero"`, `"saturated"`, `"no_data"`, `"failed"`;
  see section 6).

Two messages bracket the run: one line at the start and a summary at the end (pairs by status, median dS,
sequences that were left out). They are messages, so `suppressMessages()` hides them.

## Other methods

`dnds_est.method` chooses the method. Li's method is computed with `seqinr::kaks()`:

```{r dnds-li}
li20 <- dNdS(q20, s20, dnds_est.method = "Li")
head(li20[, c("query_id", "subject_id", "dN", "dS", "dNdS", "status")], 5)
```

The methods of KaKs_Calculator (`"NG"`, `"LWL"`, `"LPB"`, `"MLWL"`, `"MLPB"`, `"YN"`, `"MYN"`, `"GY"`, `"GMYN"`,
`"MS"`, `"MA"`, `"ALL"`) run the KaKs_Calculator program, unless `kaks_tool = "coal"` hands the seven methods NG ...
MYN to COAL:

```{r dnds-yn, eval = has_diamond && has_kaks}
yn20 <- dNdS(q20, s20, dnds_est.method = "YN")
head(yn20[, c("query_id", "subject_id", "dN", "dS", "dNdS", "status")], 5)
```

```{r dnds-yn-coal, eval = has_diamond && has_kaks && has_coalr}
yn20_coal <- dNdS(q20, s20, dnds_est.method = "YN", kaks_tool = "coal")
all.equal(yn20$dS, yn20_coal$dS)       # KaKs_Calculator prints 6 significant digits; COAL keeps all of them
max(abs(yn20$dNdS - yn20_coal$dNdS), na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Saturation and NA

A dN or dS of `NA` is not a failure of the program: for very divergent sequences the correction for multiple
substitutions at a site is not defined (the logarithm in the formula gets a negative argument), so the number of
substitutions cannot be estimated. Such a pair has status `"saturated"`. orthologr returns `NA` there (0.4.3
returned a finite, too small value), and the KaKs_Calculator methods' capped values (99, ...) are `NA` too. The
1,000-gene example has a few:

```{r dnds-1000}
q1k <- system.file("seqs/ortho_thal_cds_1000.fasta", package = "orthologr")
s1k <- system.file("seqs/ortho_lyra_cds_1000.fasta", package = "orthologr")
time_default <- system.time(res1k <- dNdS(q1k, s1k))
table(res1k$status)
subset(res1k, status != "ok")[, c("query_id", "subject_id", "dN", "dS", "dNdS", "perc_identity", "status")]
```

This pair has only 52 % protein identity: too many differences for Comeron's correction, so dN, dS and dN/dS are
all `NA`. A pair saturated at synonymous sites only usually still has its dN. A pair with status `"dS_zero"` has
no synonymous change at all: dS is 0, dN is estimated, and the ratio is `NA` because it is not defined.

The messages under the run say that 12 *A. lyrata* sequences were trimmed to a multiple of 3 and that 2 pairs have
ambiguous bases (N), whose codons were not compared; the attributes `trimmed_sequences` and
`ambiguous_sequences` list them.

## Cores and chunks

`comp_cores` spreads the gene pairs over R processes (with the default engine; on Windows one process is used).
The results do not depend on it. PAL2NAL and KaKs_Calculator are started once per chunk of up to 100 pairs rather
than once per pair (`options(orthologr.batch_tools = FALSE)` goes back to one process per pair, again with the same
results).

To compare two result tables, compare their columns: the attributes differ by design (the record of the run
holds the arguments, here `comp_cores`).

```{r same-columns}
# every column identical (names, types, values, order of rows); attributes ignored
same_columns <- function(x, y) identical(names(x), names(y)) && all(mapply(identical, x, y))
```

From here on the messages of runs that repeat an earlier one are not shown (`message = FALSE`).

```{r dnds-cores, message = FALSE}
time_2cores <- system.time(res1k_2 <- dNdS(q1k, s1k, comp_cores = 2))
same_columns(res1k, res1k_2)
rbind(`1 core` = time_default, `2 cores` = time_2cores)[, "elapsed"]
```

## Settings of orthologr 0.4.3

Version 0.5.0 changed several defaults (best hits by bit score, DIAMOND's default sensitivity, BLOSUM62 pairwise
alignments, `NA` for saturation, the `status` column, ...). The vignette "Upgrading from 0.4.3" lists each with
its measured effect. One call restores them all, for example to reproduce an old analysis:

```{r legacy}
old <- orthologr_legacy_options()
leg20 <- dNdS(q20, s20)
names(leg20)[ncol(leg20)]     # no status column under the old settings
options(old)                  # back to the current defaults
```

Only the default engine reproduces 0.4.3's numbers; `engine = "coal"` warns under these settings.

# 4. Part 2: COAL inside orthologr

## The codon alignments are the same

When coalr is installed, `dNdS()` already uses COAL for the codon alignments (`codon_aln_tool = NULL` picks
`"coal"`), because it gives the same alignments without starting Perl. The single step can be compared directly
with `codon_aln()`:

```{r codon-aln, eval = has_coalr && has_perl}
aln <- system.file("seqs/aa_seqs.aln", package = "orthologr")      # a protein alignment (CLUSTAL)
nuc <- system.file("seqs/dna_seqs.fasta", package = "orthologr")   # the CDS of the same genes
p <- codon_aln(aln, nuc, tool = "pal2nal", get_aln = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
k <- codon_aln(aln, nuc, tool = "coal", get_aln = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
identical(p$seq, k$seq)
substr(k$seq[[1]], 1, 60)
```

and in a whole run:

```{r dnds-pal2nal, eval = has_diamond && has_coalr && has_perl, message = FALSE}
time_pal2nal <- system.time(res1k_pal <- dNdS(q1k, s1k, codon_aln_tool = "pal2nal"))
same_columns(res1k_pal, res1k)
```

## `engine = "coal"`: the batched fast path

With `engine = "coal"` orthologr still runs its own DIAMOND search, then hands all gene pairs to COAL in one call.
The table has the same columns and attributes:

```{r dnds-coal, eval = has_diamond && has_coalr, message = FALSE}
time_coal <- system.time(coal1k <- dNdS(q1k, s1k, engine = "coal"))
identical(names(coal1k), names(res1k))
table(coal1k$status)
```

The table is identical to the default engine's, column for column: the protein alignments are scored as `pairwise_aln()` scores them
(`aa_aln_scoring = "pwalign"`, the default), the codon alignments are PAL2NAL's, and COAL's Comeron is a port of
orthologr's:

```{r dnds-coal-compare, eval = has_diamond && has_coalr}
same_columns(coal1k, res1k)
```

And the time (elapsed seconds of the whole call, DIAMOND included; this machine was shared with other jobs, so
take the ratios as indicative):

```{r timing-1k, eval = has_diamond && has_coalr && has_perl, message = FALSE}
time_coal2 <- system.time(dNdS(q1k, s1k, engine = "coal", comp_cores = 2))
round(rbind(`default (COAL codon step)` = time_default,
            `codon_aln_tool = "pal2nal"` = time_pal2nal,
            `engine = "coal"` = time_coal,
            `engine = "coal", 2 threads` = time_coal2)[, c("user.self", "elapsed")], 1)
```

`dNdS_coal()` is the same function under its own name, with one difference: its default method is `"YN"` (Yang and
Nielsen 2000), where `dNdS()` (also with `engine = "coal"`) defaults to `"Comeron"`. Several methods can be computed
in one call; the result then has a row per gene pair and method:

```{r dnds-coal-methods, eval = has_diamond && has_coalr}
m <- dNdS_coal(q20, s20, dnds_est.method = c("Comeron", "NG", "YN", "MYN"))
table(m$method)
head(m[order(m$query_id), c("query_id", "method", "dN", "dS", "dNdS", "status")], 8)
```

What `engine = "coal"` changes, in short:

- **speed**: no Perl or KaKs_Calculator process, no files per pair, several threads;
- **the same values** for the same pairs, for every method it has;
- **methods**: Comeron, Li, NG, LWL, MLWL, LPB, MLPB, YN, MYN. GY, GMYN, MS, MA and ALL are KaKs_Calculator's only
  (with the default engine). coalr 0.6.0 also has its own GY (maximum likelihood), but orthologr does not offer it
  through `engine = "coal"`; call `coalr::coal_dnds_pairs()` for it (below);
- **status `"no_data"`** for a pair without comparable codons, and `"saturated"` for a YN / MYN iteration that did
  not converge (KaKs_Calculator does not report this);
- `aa_aln_type`, `aa_aln_tool`, `codon_aln_tool`, `kaks_tool` and `store_locally` are ignored; `ortho_detection`
  must be `"RBH"` or `"BH"`.

## GY through coalr directly

The ortholog pairs that orthologr found can be passed to coalr as they are. `coal_dnds_pairs()` takes the CDS (file
names, or the table of `read.cds()`), the pairs, and the methods. Give it `preset = "pwalign"`: coalr's own default
protein alignment scoring is EMBOSS needle's (gap extension 0.5, free end gaps), not the one orthologr uses, so
without it some pairs get other alignments and slightly other values.

```{r coalr-gy, eval = has_diamond && has_coalr_gy}
pairs20 <- as.data.frame(res20[, c("query_id", "subject_id")])
gy <- coalr::coal_dnds_pairs(q20, s20, pairs = pairs20, methods = c("YN", "GY"), preset = "pwalign")
head(gy[, c("seq1", "method", "dN", "dS", "dNdS", "status")], 6)
# coalr's YN is orthologr's YN with engine = "coal" (same alignments, same code)
identical(gy$dS[gy$method == "YN"], dNdS_coal(q20, s20, dnds_est.method = "YN", print_citation = FALSE)$dS)
```

The same pairs with KaKs_Calculator's GY (default engine):

```{r kaks-gy, eval = has_diamond && has_coalr_gy && has_kaks}
gy_kc <- dNdS(q20, s20, dnds_est.method = "GY")
cmp <- merge(gy[gy$method == "GY", c("seq1", "dS", "dNdS")], gy_kc[, c("query_id", "dS", "dNdS")],
             by.x = "seq1", by.y = "query_id", suffixes = c("_coal", "_kaks"))
head(cmp, 5)
summary(abs(cmp$dNdS_coal - cmp$dNdS_kaks))
```

The two implement the same model (Goldman and Yang 1994, F3x4 codon frequencies) but are different programs. For
some pairs they agree to KaKs_Calculator's six printed digits; for others they differ by up to about 0.05 in dN/dS.
COAL's documentation (`docs/kaks.md`, "GY: maximum likelihood") gives the reasons: KaKs_Calculator bounds the
branch length at 3 substitutions per codon and omega at 0.001 (see AT1G01050.1 above, a pair without
nonsynonymous change: COAL reports omega 1e-6, KaKs_Calculator 0.001), and starts kappa and omega at random
values, so its maximum is not always the highest one. COAL's GY is deterministic.

## Orthogroups of more than two species

`orthogroups()` builds groups of orthologs for 2 to N species from one all-against-all DIAMOND search (reciprocal
best hits, joined into connected components), or from DeepClust clusters (`method = "deepclust"`).
`dNdS_orthogroups()` then estimates dN/dS for every pair of genes of different species within each group. With
`engine = "coal"` COAL threads the codons onto one multiple alignment per group (Clustal Omega by default) and
estimates all pairs in process. The package's protein example has four Brassicaceae:

```{r orthogroups-small}
files <- c(Athaliana = system.file("seqs/example_athal_aa.faa", package = "orthologr"),
           Alyrata   = system.file("seqs/example_alyra_aa.faa", package = "orthologr"),
           Brapa     = system.file("seqs/example_brapa_aa.faa", package = "orthologr"),
           Thalophila = system.file("seqs/example_thalo_aa.faa", package = "orthologr"))
og4 <- orthogroups(files, seq_type = "protein")
og4
```

These are proteins, so there is no dN/dS for them; section 5 runs `dNdS_orthogroups()` on the CDS of four
bacteria.

## DeepClust clusters

`dNdS_clusters()` estimates dN/dS for all pairs within DIAMOND DeepClust clusters of one or more CDS files (it runs
`deepclust()` when no clusters are given) and summarises each cluster. It always uses COAL:

```{r clusters-small, eval = has_diamond && has_coalr}
cl20 <- dNdS_clusters(c(q20, s20), aa_aln_tool = "pairwise")
head(cl20$summary[, c("cluster_id", "n_members", "method", "n_pairs", "n_ok", "dS_median", "dNdS_median")])
```

# 5. Part 3: a worked example on four Chlamydia genomes

COAL's tutorials use the coding sequences of four Chlamydia genomes from NCBI RefSeq: two strains of *C.
trachomatis* (D/UW-3/CX and L2/434/Bu, very close), *C. muridarum* (Nigg; a sister species that infects mice) and
*C. pneumoniae* (CWL029; distant). Each has about 900 to 1,050 genes. The chunks of this section run when the
environment variable `ORTHOLOGR_TUTORIAL_DATA` names a folder for the files (which is how this document was made);
the package build does not set it.

## Getting the data

```{r get-data, eval = get_genomes}
genomes <- data.frame(
  file = c("ctrachomatis_D.cds.fna.gz", "ctrachomatis_L2.cds.fna.gz",
           "cmuridarum_Nigg.cds.fna.gz", "cpneumoniae_CWL029.cds.fna.gz"),
  path = c("GCF/000/008/725/GCF_000008725.1_ASM872v1",  "GCF/000/068/585/GCF_000068585.1_ASM6858v1",
           "GCF/000/006/685/GCF_000006685.1_ASM668v1",  "GCF/000/008/745/GCF_000008745.1_ASM874v1"),
  md5  = c("5b011994dd999e140e6f6686d1c0265d", "45521c789e56723398b470750e7891b9",
           "fa60229127c9a08cbb1a421bf0aa9cd5", "6c8cf86b9291ec57fbcf99a86de3366b"))
dir.create(tut_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(genomes))) {
  dest <- file.path(tut_dir, genomes$file[i])
  if (!file.exists(dest))
    download.file(paste0("https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/", genomes$path[i], "/",
                         basename(genomes$path[i]), "_cds_from_genomic.fna.gz"), dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  stopifnot(unname(tools::md5sum(dest)) == genomes$md5[i])
}
cds <- setNames(file.path(tut_dir, genomes$file), c("ctrD", "ctrL2", "cmu", "cpn"))
sapply(cds, function(f) length(Biostrings::fasta.seqlengths(f)))
```

(COAL has the same download as a shell script, `docs/tutorials/data/get_chlamydia.sh`, which checks SHA-256
checksums.) orthologr reads gzipped FASTA directly.

## One species pair, both engines

*C. trachomatis* D against *C. muridarum*, with the default engine and with COAL:

```{r chl-pair, eval = get_genomes}
t_default <- system.time(ct_cm <- dNdS(cds["ctrD"], cds["cmu"]))
```

The messages are worth reading once: RefSeq CDS files contain a few sequences whose length is not a multiple of 3
(trimmed), some with ambiguous bases, and some with internal stop codons (pseudogenes); all are listed in the
attributes of the result. The same with COAL, on one and on two threads:

```{r chl-pair-coal, eval = get_genomes, message = FALSE}
t_coal  <- system.time(ct_cm_coal <- dNdS(cds["ctrD"], cds["cmu"], engine = "coal"))
t_coal2 <- system.time(dNdS(cds["ctrD"], cds["cmu"], engine = "coal", comp_cores = 2))
same_columns(ct_cm, ct_cm_coal)
round(rbind(default = t_default, coal = t_coal, `coal, 2 threads` = t_coal2)[, c("user.self", "elapsed")], 1)
```

`user.self` is the CPU time of the R process itself (DIAMOND, PAL2NAL and other programs it starts are not in it);
`elapsed` is the wall-clock time of the whole call. The search is a large part of the time at this size (about
900 genes): COAL's share is a fraction of a second.

## Reading the results

```{r chl-status, eval = get_genomes}
table(ct_cm$status)
summary(ct_cm$dS)
summary(ct_cm$dNdS)
```

How to read this:

- **dS** is the estimated number of synonymous substitutions per synonymous site. A median of 0.93 means that
  *C. trachomatis* and *C. muridarum* differ at almost one change per synonymous site: in the upper part of the
  range where pairwise estimates still work (up to about 1, at most 1.5 - 2), with a quarter of the genes above
  1.06. For comparison, the two *C. trachomatis* strains differ by a dS of about 0.01 (section "orthogroups"
  below) and *A. thaliana* / *A. lyrata* by 0.13.
- **dN/dS** has a median of 0.077: nonsynonymous sites change at about a thirteenth of the rate of synonymous
  sites. Most genes are under strong purifying selection; none has a ratio above 1 over its whole length (the
  maximum is 0.61). A ratio averaged over a whole gene rarely exceeds 1 even when a few sites are under positive
  selection; site models (codeml, HyPhy) are needed for those.
- **8 pairs are saturated**: dN or dS cannot be estimated; they are `NA`, not 0.

The genes with the highest dN/dS among the well-estimated pairs (dS between 0.05 and 1, at least 100 aligned
amino acids), with the gene names from the FASTA headers:

```{r chl-top, eval = get_genomes}
hdr <- names(Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(cds["ctrD"]))
tag <- function(h, key) ifelse(grepl(paste0("[", key, "="), h, fixed = TRUE),
                                sub(paste0(".*\\[", key, "=([^]]+)\\].*"), "\\1", h), NA)
gene <- setNames(ifelse(is.na(tag(hdr, "gene")), tag(hdr, "locus_tag"), tag(hdr, "gene")), sub(" .*", "", hdr))
product <- setNames(tag(hdr, "protein"), sub(" .*", "", hdr))
ok <- subset(ct_cm, status == "ok" & dS >= 0.05 & dS <= 1 & alig_length >= 100)
ok$gene <- gene[ok$query_id]
ok$product <- substr(product[ok$query_id], 1, 40)
head(ok[order(-ok$dNdS), c("gene", "product", "dN", "dS", "dNdS", "perc_identity", "alig_length")], 8)
```

The top of the list is what one expects of an obligate intracellular bacterium: an inclusion membrane protein
(CT_228; Inc proteins sit in the membrane of the vacuole the bacterium lives in, in contact with the host) and
several hypothetical proteins, next to a few enzymes. Short alignments were left out on purpose: without the length
filter the top of the list is dominated by alignments of 50 - 100 amino acids, whose ratios are the noisiest.

## Filtering

`filter_dNdS()` keeps the pairs with dN/dS below a threshold (default 2) and leaves out pairs whose dS is 0 or
`NA`:

```{r chl-filter, eval = get_genomes}
filtered <- filter_dNdS(ct_cm)
c(all = nrow(ct_cm), kept = nrow(filtered))
```

For gene-by-gene interpretation a stricter filter is common: enough codons and dS in a range where it is estimated
well (COAL's tutorials use 0.05 <= dS <= 1 and at least 100 compared codons as a start; here the length of the
DIAMOND alignment, in amino acids, stands in for the number of codons):

```{r chl-strict, eval = get_genomes}
strict <- subset(ct_cm, status == "ok" & dS >= 0.05 & dS <= 1 & alig_length >= 100)
nrow(strict)
median(strict$dNdS)
```

## Saturation: a distant species

*C. pneumoniae* is far from *C. trachomatis*. The same call gives many saturated pairs and a high median dS, and
the summary message says that the species are too distant for pairwise dN/dS:

```{r chl-distant, eval = get_genomes}
ct_cp <- dNdS(cds["ctrD"], cds["cpn"], engine = "coal")
table(ct_cp$status)
summary(ct_cp$dS)
```

A dS above about 1.5 to 2 means that most synonymous sites have changed more than once: the estimates are dominated
by the correction for multiple hits and are noisy, and ratios computed from them are not reliable. Use closer
species (or a phylogenetic method over many species, such as codeml or HyPhy) for such comparisons.

## More than two species: orthogroups

`orthogroups()` and `dNdS_orthogroups()` report every trimmed sequence in a block of messages per file; to keep
this document short only their summary lines are shown, with this helper:

```{r summary-lines, eval = get_genomes}
summary_lines <- function(expr, pattern = "^(orthogroups|dNdS_orthogroups)\\(\\)|^Note: [0-9]") {
  msgs <- character()
  value <- withCallingHandlers(expr, message = function(m) {
    msgs <<- c(msgs, conditionMessage(m)); invokeRestart("muffleMessage") })
  message(paste(grep(pattern, msgs, value = TRUE), collapse = ""), appendLF = FALSE)
  value
}
```

```{r chl-og, eval = get_genomes}
og <- summary_lines(orthogroups(cds))
og
```

```{r chl-og-dnds, eval = get_genomes && has_clustalo}
t_ogd <- system.time(og_dnds <- summary_lines(dNdS_orthogroups(og, cds_files = cds, engine = "coal")))
t_ogd[["elapsed"]]
table(og_dnds$pairs$status)
head(og_dnds$summary)
```

The median dS of each pair of species within the single-copy orthogroups orders the species as expected:

```{r chl-og-species, eval = get_genomes && has_clustalo}
pr <- og_dnds$pairs
pr$species_pair <- paste(pr$query_species, pr$subject_species, sep = " - ")
aggregate(dS ~ species_pair, data = pr, FUN = median)
table(pr$species_pair, pr$status)
```

The two *C. trachomatis* strains differ by a median dS of 0.009: so close that many of their pairs have no
synonymous difference at all (status `"dS_zero"`). *C. trachomatis* against *C. muridarum* gives 1.29 here
(method YN, the default of `dNdS_orthogroups()`, on one Clustal Omega alignment per group) against 0.93 with
Comeron's method on pairwise alignments above: different methods disagree most where dS is large. Every pair with
*C. pneumoniae* is beyond 2, mostly saturated. The summary message's warning that "the two species are probably too
distant" refers to the pooled pairs of all species; here it is the *C. pneumoniae* pairs that are.

## Divergence stratigraphy

`divergence_stratigraphy()` assigns each gene of a query species a divergence stratum: the decile of its dS among
the orthologs to a subject species (genes with dN/dS above `dnds.threshold` are left out):

```{r chl-ds, eval = get_genomes, message = FALSE}
ds <- divergence_stratigraphy(cds["ctrD"], cds["cmu"])
head(ds)
table(ds$DS)
```

The strata are deciles, so they hold equal numbers of genes by construction: stratum 1 holds the tenth of the genes
with the smallest dS (the most conserved at synonymous sites), stratum 10 the most diverged. The strata are the
input of `myTAI`-style analyses that ask whether, for example, genes expressed at a stage of development are
younger or more diverged than others.

# 6. Choosing a method, saturation, reproducibility, troubleshooting

## Choosing a method

- **Comeron** (default): fast, no external program; a good default for pairs of moderately diverged species.
- **YN** (Yang and Nielsen 2000) and **MYN**: account for the transition / transversion bias and codon frequencies;
  the usual choice when a reviewer asks for "a model-based estimate"; compute them with `engine = "coal"` or
  `kaks_tool = "coal"` if KaKs_Calculator is not installed.
- **NG**, **LWL**, **LPB**, **MLWL**, **MLPB**, **Li**: counting methods; mostly for comparison with older studies.
- **GY**, **GMYN**, **MS**, **MA**: maximum likelihood and model selection / averaging in KaKs_Calculator; much
  slower (MS and MA several seconds per pair).

For closely related species the methods agree closely; they differ most where dS is large, which is where no
pairwise method is reliable. Compare two methods on your own data before choosing (as `dNdS_coal()` does above
in one call).

## Saturation and NA, in one place

| `status` | dN | dS | dNdS | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `"ok"` | value | value | value | estimated |
| `"dS_zero"` | value | 0 | `NA` | no synonymous change: the ratio is not defined |
| `"saturated"` | value or `NA` | `NA` (usually) | `NA` | too many differences for the correction of multiple hits |
| `"no_data"` | `NA` | `NA` | `NA` | no codons to compare (engine COAL) |
| `"failed"` | `NA` | `NA` | `NA` | a step failed; reason in `attr(result, "failed_pairs")` |

Do not replace `NA` by 0 or by a large number: both are wrong. Leave such pairs out (`filter_dNdS()`) and report how
many there were.

## Reproducibility

Every result carries a record of its run: the package version, all arguments, every `orthologr.*` option in force,
the engine, the versions of the programs, and the size and MD5 checksum of the input files.

```{r record}
run <- attr(res1k, "orthologr_run")
names(run)
run$orthologr
run$status_counts
```

`write_dNdS()` writes the table with this record (as `<file>.run.json`, needs jsonlite) and `read_dNdS()` reads
both back:

```{r write-read, eval = has_diamond && requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)}
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
write_dNdS(res1k, f)
back <- read_dNdS(f)
all.equal(as.data.frame(back), as.data.frame(res1k), check.attributes = FALSE)
unlink(c(f, paste0(f, ".run.json")))
```

Results do not depend on `comp_cores` or on whether COAL builds the codon alignments. In a methods section, give
the versions of orthologr, coalr (if used), DIAMOND and KaKs_Calculator, the method and the engine.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `DIAMOND was not found. Run diamond_install() ...` | install DIAMOND (`diamond_install()`), or pass `aligner_path` |
| `engine = "coal" ... needs the package coalr` / class `orthologr_error_package_missing` | install coalr (section 2) |
| `dNdS_coal() computes dnds_est.method = ...; "GY" is only available with engine = "orthologr"` | GY, GMYN, MS, MA and ALL need KaKs_Calculator and the default engine (or use coalr's GY directly) |
| a warning of class `orthologr_warning_coal_version` | the installed coalr predates COAL's Comeron rule of 0.6.0; reinstall coalr |
| many `"saturated"` pairs, a message that the species are too distant | expected for distant species (section 5): choose closer species |
| a warning that a file seems to hold several transcripts per gene | keep one transcript per gene first, e.g. with `retrieve_longest_isoforms()` |
| pairs with status `"failed"` | `attr(result, "failed_pairs")` gives the program and its message |
| sequences missing from the result | `attr(result, "dropped_sequences")` and `attr(result, "trimmed_sequences")` list them with the reason |
| you need the intermediate files | `options(orthologr.keep_tmp = "some/folder")` keeps them |

Errors and warnings have classes (`orthologr_error_tool_missing`, `_package_missing`, `_bad_input`,
`_bad_argument`, ...), so they can be caught with `tryCatch()`:

```{r errors}
tryCatch(dNdS(q20, s20, dnds_est.method = "YNN"),
         orthologr_error_bad_argument = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
```
